sections.title: Foreword / scope
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE is an XML exchange format for STATIC road networks (roads, lanes, junctions, objects along roads, signals) for driving simulation. Dynamic content (traffic, scenarios) is out of scope and belongs to OpenSCENARIO.
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9.0 deliverables add a Junction guideline 1.0.0 and a Signal reference 1.0.0 document next to the specification.

sections.title: Deliverables
sections.summary: The standard ships as a file-format specification, XML schemas (XSD), a UML model, sample files (use cases/examples), example implementations, a reference implementation for spirals (odrSpiral) and a signal catalog.

use_cases.how: Validate generated .xodr against the official XSD of the targeted revMinor; use the sample files (e.g. Ex_Line-Spiral-Arc.xodr) as regression inputs.
Mirror the ASAM odrSpiral reference implementation (Fresnel integrals) so OdrForge evaluates clothoids identically to other tools.

right: Treat the UML model and 'Rules' sections as normative; XML examples are only illustrative.
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 deliverable list: specification (HTML), Junction guideline, Signal reference, Enterprise Architect UML model, XSD files, examples, implementation examples, release presentation.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE files (.xodr) describe road geometry plus logic-relevant features (lanes, signals) of synthetic or real road networks so they can be fed into simulators and exchanged between tools. Every node can be extended with user-defined data while keeping interoperability.

sections.title: Normative vs non-normative
sections.summary: Modal-verb statements (requirements/permissions/prohibitions), UML diagrams of the model, and 'Rules' sections are normative. XML examples and use-case descriptions are non-normative.
right: When text and an XML example disagree, follow the normative text/UML/rules.
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8/1.9 restructure into ISO-like chapters (Scope, Normative references, Terms, Abbreviations, Backward compatibility); notes, footnotes, examples and sequence diagrams are explicitly informative and must not contain requirements.

sections.title: Naming conventions
sections.summary: Data types follow IEEE (double = IEEE 754 binary64).

sections.title: Units
sections.summary: All numeric values are SI unless stated otherwise: m, rad, s, m/s. Geographic positions use the unit of the spatial reference system (e.g. degrees for WGS84/EPSG:4326). A small set of explicit unit identifiers exists only for signage and speed indication.

rules.text: The optional explicit units are to be used only for signage and speed indication.
Explicit units must not be used as general units, e.g. for road geometry.
If no unit is given (or there is no way to state one), SI units apply.

use_cases.how: OSM 'maxspeed=50' (km/h) or '30 mph': either convert to m/s, or keep the value and set @unit='km/h'/'mph' on <speed>; never put km/h into geometry fields.

right: Store all angles (hdg, roll, pitch) in radians; convert OSM/degree inputs.
Use @unit on speed/signal values when preserving the posted number.
wrong: Using km or ft for geometry lengths, s-coordinates or widths: geometry is always meters.
Writing degrees into hdg.

sections.title: Modal verbs
sections.summary: shall/shall not = requirement (no deviation); should/should not = recommendation; may/need not = permission; can/can not = capability; must/must not = external obligation not enforced by OpenDRIVE.
right: Map 'shall' rules to validator errors and 'should' rules to warnings in OdrForge's checker.

sections.title: Typographic and UML conventions
sections.summary: <element> denotes an XML element and @attribute an attribute. Class diagrams follow UML (ISO TS 19103 notation); optional attributes are marked [0..1], mandatory ones have no marker. Colors: orange = diagram entry class, yellow = package of current chapter, blue = other package, green = geometry-bearing classes.
figures: Figure 1: UML notation (associations, roles, multiplicities) per ISO TS 19103 - read multiplicities to know required children.
Figure 2: UML attribute notation - '[0..1]' after an attribute means optional; no marker means mandatory (must be written).

sections.title: Use of IDs
sections.summary: IDs must be unique within their class (e.g. all road ids, all junction ids), lane ids must be unique within a lane section, and only IDs that are defined may be referenced.
concepts: lane id unique per lane section

rules.text: IDs are unique within a class (road ids among roads, junction ids among junctions, etc.).
Lane IDs are unique within one lane section.
Only IDs that are actually defined may be referenced (no dangling references).

use_cases.how: OSM ways split into several roads need distinct OpenDRIVE road ids; keep a deterministic mapping table and verify every road/junction/signal/controller reference resolves.

right: Allocate ids per class from a counter or stable hash; a road and a junction may share the same numeric id (different classes) but avoiding that eases debugging.
Run a post-write pass checking that all predecessor/successor/junction/connectingRoad/signal references exist.
wrong: Reusing an id for two roads; referencing a road id that was later dropped (e.g. after filtering short ways).

sections.title: Curvature
sections.summary: Curvature = 1/radius. Positive curvature is a left curve (counter-clockwise when driving in +s), negative is a right curve (clockwise).

formulas.name: curvature definition
formulas.expr: k = 1/R ; k > 0 left (CCW), k < 0 right (CW)
formulas.notes: Sign is relative to the +s direction of the reference line, not the driving direction.

formulas.name: heading/curvature relation
formulas.expr: dhdg/ds = k(s)
formulas.notes: Holds for every planView element (implicit in arc/spiral definitions); used to derive heading from curvature integrals.

right: Compute curvature sign w.r.t. the reference-line direction you chose; if you reverse a road, negate all curvatures.
wrong: Taking OSM turning direction relative to traffic flow when the reference line runs against the traffic.

sections.title: Positioning within ASAM
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE (static road network) combines with OpenCRG (detailed road surface) and OpenSCENARIO (dynamic content: traffic, maneuvers) to form a complete scenario-based simulation description.
figures: Figure 3: relation between OpenDRIVE, OpenCRG, OpenSCENARIO - OpenDRIVE + OpenCRG are static, OpenSCENARIO adds dynamics.

sections.title: Backward compatibility
sections.summary: 1.7.0 is backward compatible with 1.6.1. Elements introduced in 1.5 that are incompatible with 1.4 are optional in the 1.7 schema and annotated 'Optional for backwards compatibility'. Compatibility to 1.4/1.5 is defined against their documentation, not their (erroneous) XSDs.
right: A 1.7 reader should accept 1.6.x files; when writing, still emit the 'optional for backward compatibility' elements since modern consumers expect them.
wrong: Relying on 1.4/1.5 XSD quirks; those XSDs had errors relative to their documents.
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8.0 is backward compatible with 1.7.0 (minor release: adds features, deprecates unused ones, keeps all 1.7 features).

1.9.0 is backward compatible with 1.8.1; 1.9 adds lane layers (permanent/temporary), @temporary/@invalidated for objects and signals, <curveLocal> outlines, signal semantics vehicle/person/animal, OpenCRG global-mode x/y/z/h offsets; 'bounding box' renamed 'bounding volume'.
1.9 cautions against using lane-layer files with scenario specs that do not know layers (e.g. OpenSCENARIO XML <= 1.3.1).

sections.title: References to other standards
sections.summary: XML 1.0 Schema, UML 2.5.1, ISO 3166-2 country codes, ISO 8855 right-handed vehicle coordinate systems, ISO 8601 date/time, georeferencing per ISO 19111 (EPSG/PROJ), ASAM OpenCRG.
right: Use ISO 3166-2 codes for signal @country, ISO 8601 for header @date, PROJ strings for geoReference.

sections.title: File structure
sections.summary: Data is stored in XML files with extension .xodr; gzip-compressed files use .xodrz. Elements form levels (level-1 children of <OpenDRIVE> are 'primary elements'); every element can carry user data. All floats are IEEE 754 doubles and must be printed so they round-trip.

formulas.name: float output precision
formulas.expr: printf("%.17g", value)  // or shortest round-trip algorithm (Ryu/Grisu/std::to_chars)
formulas.notes: Guarantees bit-exact round trip; readers should use a correct parsing algorithm (e.g. strtod / std::from_chars).

rules.text: Writers use a correct shortest round-trip float printer or always emit 17 significant digits.
Readers use a correct accuracy-preserving float parser.

use_cases.how: Use std::to_chars (shortest round-trip) or %.17g for x, y, hdg, length, s and polynomial coefficients so that geometry continuity checks pass after re-reading.

right: std::to_chars / %.17g for every double.
Optionally support writing .xodrz via gzip.
wrong: Printing with %.3f or default iostream precision (6 digits): breaks s-sum and continuity, especially with large UTM coordinates.
changes_1_8_1_9: Unchanged in 1.8/1.9 (moved to section 6.1).

sections.title: Combining files (<include>)
sections.summary: An <include> element makes the reader immediately parse the referenced file in place. The included file repeats the parent element as its root (e.g. <planView> containing <geometry>s). Consistency between included content and context is the author's responsibility.
concepts: same parent element in both files

attributes.name: file
attributes.meaning: Location (path/URI) of the file to include

rules.text: Readers start reading the included file immediately when the <include> element is parsed.
The parent element of <include> is present both in the including file and as root of the included file.

right: Included planview.xml has <planView> as root, mirroring the parent in the main file.
wrong: Including a file whose root does not match the parent element; including content inconsistent with context (e.g. geometry s values not continuing).

sections.title: Overview of elements
sections.summary: Tree: <OpenDRIVE> -> <header> (<geoReference>, <offset>), <road> (planView/geometry, link, type/speed, elevationProfile, lateralProfile, lanes, objects, signals, surface, railroad), <controller>, <junction>, <junctionGroup>, <station>.

rules.text: Exactly one <OpenDRIVE> root and exactly one <header>; at least one <road> (UML multiplicity road 1..*); controller, junction, junctionGroup, station 0..*.

changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 root element table lists no attributes; namespace/children are defined in the XSD and UML.
1.8 adds <header> children <license> and <defaultRegulations>; 1.9 adds lane layers etc. (other chapters).
figures: Figure 4 (UML Core): t_OpenDRIVE has header 1, road 1..*, controller/junction/junctionGroup/station 0..*; every element derives from _OpenDriveElement which may hold g_additionalData (userData 0..*, include 0..*, dataQuality 0..1).

sections.title: Attributes
sections.summary: All attributes are annotated in the UML model with unit (per Units), type (primitive like string/double or complex/enum type) and value range. Derived double types: t_grZero (>0), t_grEqZero (>=0), t_zeroOne ([0,1]).
wrong: Emitting geometry @length = 0 (violates t_grZero) for degenerate OSM segments - drop or merge them instead.
Negative s values.

sections.title: Header
sections.summary: <header> is the first child of <OpenDRIVE> (exactly one). It carries format revision, metadata, bounding box in inertial coordinates, and optional <geoReference> and <offset>.

attributes.name: spdxid
attributes.meaning: SPDX identifier/expression; custom licenses use LicenseRef- prefix

attributes.name: type
attributes.meaning: Road type the default regulation (speed/priority) applies to

rules.text: <header> is the very first element inside <OpenDRIVE> and occurs exactly once.
Inside <defaultRegulations> only <speed> and <priority> elements are used.
<signalRegulations> is used for signs that change driving rules (e.g. turn-on-red).
<signalRegulations> is not to be used as a signal catalogue.

use_cases.case: OSM import from a UTM-projected extract
use_cases.how: revMajor=1, revMinor=7 (or the targeted version), date=now ISO 8601, north/south/east/west = bounding box of all geometry in the (offset-reduced) inertial frame, vendor='OdrForge', plus geoReference and offset.
Emit <license name='Open Database License 1.0' spdxid='ODbL-1.0' resource='https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/'/>.

right: Set revMinor to match the schema features actually used (no 1.8 elements in a revMinor=7 file).
Compute north/south/east/west from the final sampled geometry including lane widths if possible.
wrong: Header not first; two headers; revMinor=7 with <license> (1.8 element).

1.9 table types revMajor/revMinor as integer; content otherwise unchanged; geoReference/offset described in section 8.5.

sections.title: Traffic direction
sections.summary: Unless otherwise stated, the spec assumes right-hand traffic in all examples, figures and descriptions.

sections.title: Additional data overview
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE may embed external/ancillary data anywhere (group g_additionalData on every _OpenDriveElement): userData, include, dataQuality (and layout sets). Processing is application-specific.
figures: Figure 4 (UML Core): g_additionalData on every element = userData 0..*, include 0..*, dataQuality 0..1; dataQuality has error 0..1 and rawData 0..1.

sections.title: User data
sections.summary: <userData> carries data not (yet) modelled in OpenDRIVE or needed by a specific application (e.g. textures). It should sit next to the element it refers to and may appear on any element.

attributes.name: value
attributes.meaning: User data value (application-defined); arbitrary child content (userDataContent) also allowed

rules.text: Ancillary data is described close to the element it refers to.
<userData> may be stored at any element.

use_cases.how: Add <userData code='osm:way' value='123456'/> under <road> (and osm:node under signals/objects) for traceability and debugging.

right: Namespace codes (e.g. 'odrforge:...', 'osm:...') to avoid collisions.
wrong: Encoding information in userData that has a proper OpenDRIVE element (speed, lane type, signals) - consumers ignore userData.

sections.title: Including data
sections.summary: <include> elements may be placed anywhere and reference external files; how they are processed depends on the application (see 4.2 for parsing semantics).

attributes.name: file
attributes.meaning: Location of the file to include

changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 (7.3): included file must contain OpenDRIVE elements; reader loads it on parse; parent element must exist in both files.

sections.title: Layout types (<set>/<instance>)
sections.summary: User-generated layouts for elements such as road marks or signals can be referenced via <set> elements, each followed by one or more <instance> elements; the actual layout design lives in the application, not in OpenDRIVE.
changes_1_8_1_9: Not present in the 1.9 Additional data chapter (only userData, include, dataQuality are described) - treat as obsolete; do not emit.

sections.title: Data quality
sections.summary: <dataQuality> describes the quality/accuracy of integrated external data (e.g. GPS). <error> lists absolute/relative errors in meters; <rawData> holds metadata about the raw source.

attributes.name: xyAbsolute
attributes.meaning: Absolute error of road data in x/y

attributes.name: xyRelative
attributes.meaning: Relative error between adjacent entries in x/y

attributes.name: zRelative
attributes.meaning: Relative error between adjacent entries in z

attributes.name: date
attributes.meaning: Delivery date ISO 8601 (time of day optional)

rules.text: <dataQuality> may be stored at any position (max one per element).

use_cases.how: <dataQuality><rawData date='2026-10-01' source='custom' sourceComment='OpenStreetMap' postProcessing='processed' postProcessingComment='OdrForge fit'/><error xyAbsolute='2.0' .../></dataQuality> at header or road level.

sections.title: Coordinate systems overview
sections.summary: Three systems: inertial x/y/z, reference-line s/t/h, local u/v/z. The local system is placed relative to the reference-line system (unless stated otherwise); the reference-line system is placed in the inertial system by origin plus heading (and roll from superelevation; never pitch).
figures: Figure 5: the three coordinate systems available.
Figure 6: how they interact - local is relative to s/t/h, s/t/h relative to inertial via origin + heading/roll.

sections.title: Inertial coordinate system
sections.summary: Right-handed system per ISO 8855: x right/east, y up(drawing)/north, z out of plane/up. Objects and signals placed inertially use heading (about z), then pitch (about y'), then roll (about x'').

formulas.name: inertial rotation sequence
formulas.expr: R = Rz(heading) * Ry(pitch) * Rx(roll)   (intrinsic z, y', x'')
formulas.vars: heading about z, pitch about y', roll about x''
formulas.notes: Derived from the text: heading 0 -> x' along x (east), +pi/2 -> x' along y (north); pitch +pi/2 -> x'' = -z (positive pitch points nose DOWN, right-hand rule); roll +pi/2 -> z''' = -y''.

formulas.name: heading to direction vector
formulas.expr: dir = (cos(hdg), sin(hdg))
formulas.notes: Mathematical angle convention, NOT compass bearing.

use_cases.how: hdg = pi/2 - bearing_rad (bearing clockwise from north) and normalize.

right: Headings are counter-clockwise from east (+x), in radians.
wrong: Using compass bearing (clockwise from north) directly as hdg.
Assuming positive pitch is nose-up: with the right-hand rule about y', +pitch tilts x toward -z.
changes_1_8_1_9: Content unchanged in 1.9 (section 8.2).
figures: Figure 7: positive axes and positive angle directions of heading/pitch/roll in inertial system.
Figure 8: intermediate frames x'/y'/z after heading, x''/y'/z'' after pitch, x'''/y'''/z''' after roll.

sections.title: Reference line coordinate system
sections.summary: Right-handed s/t/h along the road reference line. s = arc length from road start measured in the x/y plane (elevation ignored); t = lateral, positive to the left; h = up, orthogonal to s/t. The reference line always lies in the inertial x/y plane; superelevation rolls the t/h axes about s; there is no pitch, and elevation does not change s.

formulas.name: reference-line point to inertial (no superelevation)
formulas.expr: x = xr(s) - t*sin(hdg(s)) ; y = yr(s) + t*cos(hdg(s)) ; z = zr(s) + h
formulas.vars: xr,yr,hdg from planView at s; zr(s) = elevation polynomial a+b*ds+c*ds^2+d*ds^3 (chapter 8)
formulas.notes: Derived from the axis definitions (t points to the left normal (-sin hdg, cos hdg)); spec gives the geometric definition, not this equation.

formulas.name: reference-line point to inertial (with superelevation roll phi)
formulas.expr: x = xr(s) - t*cos(phi)*sin(hdg) + h*sin(phi)*sin(hdg) ; y = yr(s) + t*cos(phi)*cos(hdg) - h*sin(phi)*cos(hdg) ; z = zr(s) + t*sin(phi) + h*cos(phi)
formulas.vars: phi(s) = superelevation a+b*ds+c*ds^2+d*ds^3 [rad] (chapter 8.4.2); positive phi lifts +t (left) side
formulas.notes: Derived: rotation of (t,h) about s by phi (right-hand). Matches Figures 10 and 12 (roll>0 tilts t''' upward and h toward the right).

formulas.name: s is planar arc length
formulas.expr: s = integral sqrt(x'(p)^2 + y'(p)^2) dp   (no z term)
formulas.notes: Elevation does not affect s; a sloped road's 3D length is longer than its s length.

formulas.name: local tangent / normal
formulas.expr: T = (cos hdg, sin hdg) ; N_left = (-sin hdg, cos hdg)
formulas.notes: N_left is the +t direction.

rules.text: The reference line lies in the inertial x/y plane; s is measured in that plane.
No pitch exists in s/t/h; elevation does not change s.

use_cases.how: Evaluate (xr,yr,hdg) at s, then offset by t (sum of laneOffset and lane widths) along N_left; add z from elevation (+ t*tan/ sin of superelevation).

use_cases.case: Sloped OSM road with elevation data
use_cases.how: Fit planView on 2D projected points; compute s from 2D length; store height as elevationProfile in s - never use 3D distance for s.

right: Compute all s from 2D planar lengths.
Positive t = left of reference-line direction; right lanes have negative ids and negative t.
wrong: Using 3D distance for s or geometry @length.
Treating t as positive to the right.
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 (8.3) names the roll 'superelevation' explicitly and adds: t is measured in the superelevated (tilted) surface; lane @width is not changed by superelevation, so its x/y projection is narrower (width*cos(phi)); objects/signals are NOT rotated by superelevation, but their @t follows the tilted lane so items on a lane border stay on it; object @zOffset is measured in z, 0 = local elevation at s, so to sit on a superelevated surface zOffset must include the superelevation height offset.
figures: Figure 9: s/t/h axes along the reference line.
Figure 10: rotations - heading about h (s' toward t at +pi/2), roll about s'.
Figure 11: s/t/h origin placed in inertial space by (x,y) and heading.
Figure 12: roll caused by <superelevation>: with positive roll the left (t>0) side is higher and h' tilts to the right - lesson: positive superelevation lifts the left side.
Figure 13: <elevation> projected onto the reference line: s/t stay horizontal; elevation only shifts z (no pitch).

sections.title: Local coordinate system
sections.summary: Right-handed u/v/z: unrotated u = s (forward), v = t (left), z = h (up). Objects are oriented by heading (about z), pitch (about v'), roll (about u''). The local system is positioned only by its origin in s/t/h and its heading relative to the reference line.

formulas.name: local (object) heading to inertial heading
formulas.expr: hdg_inertial = hdg_refline(s) + hdg_local
formulas.vars: hdg_local = object @hdg relative to reference line
formulas.notes: Derived from Figure 16: local heading measured from the s direction.

formulas.name: local point (u,v) to inertial
formulas.expr: P = P_st(s,t) + R(hdg_refline(s) + hdg_local) * (u, v)
formulas.vars: R(a) = [[cos a, -sin a],[sin a, cos a]]; P_st via 6.3
formulas.notes: Used for object outlines (cornerLocal) and repeated objects.

right: Object @hdg = 0 means aligned with the road's +s direction.
wrong: Giving object heading as an absolute inertial heading when the object is road-placed.
changes_1_8_1_9: Unchanged in 1.9 (8.4).
figures: Figure 14: positive axes/angles of the local system.
Figure 15: local system after heading, pitch, roll.
Figure 16: local system positioned relative to the reference-line system via origin and heading.
Figure 17: summary - inertial, reference-line and local systems used together.

sections.title: Summary of coordinate systems
sections.summary: Inertial, reference-line and local systems are used simultaneously; Figure 17 shows a typical chain.

sections.title: Georeferencing
sections.summary: <geoReference> in <header> holds a PROJ string (in CDATA) defining the spatial reference system of the inertial x/y. Use official EPSG parameter sets unchanged; UTM-like systems carry false easting/northing via +x_0/+y_0. Missing geoReference means a local Cartesian system. To avoid huge coordinates, <offset> shifts/rotates the dataset instead of editing projection parameters.

formulas.name: offset (1.9 explicit formula)
formulas.expr: xWorld = xODR*cos(hdg) - yODR*sin(hdg) + xOffset ; yWorld = xODR*sin(hdg) + yODR*cos(hdg) + yOffset ; zWorld = zODR + zOffset
formulas.vars: ODR = coordinates in the file; World = coordinates in the projected CRS of geoReference
formulas.notes: Apply before PROJ inverse to lat/lon. With hdg=0 (recommended): World = ODR + offset (Figure 18). 1.7/1.9 prose says 'translate then rotate around new origin', which reads differently from the formula - avoid ambiguity by writing hdg=0.

formulas.name: OdrForge writer choice
formulas.expr: xOffset = round(center_x), yOffset = round(center_y); xODR = xProj - xOffset; yODR = yProj - yOffset; hdg = 0
formulas.notes: Keeps file coordinates near (0,0) and exactly invertible.

rules.text: The PROJ string is marked as CDATA.
At most one projection definition; if missing, a local Cartesian system is assumed.
Use official EPSG parameter sets for PROJ strings and do not change parameters.
To apply an offset, use <offset> rather than changing projection parameters (e.g. +x_0/+y_0).
Avoid rotation about z in <offset> (hdg should be 0).
Choose <offset> so file x/y are roughly centered on (0,0) to protect float precision in consumers.

use_cases.how: Pick UTM zone of the area centroid; project with PROJ; write the EPSG-equivalent PROJ string in CDATA (e.g. '+proj=utm +zone=32 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs'); subtract the centroid as <offset x y z=0 hdg=0>.

right: Use projected metric CRS (UTM/local TM) so geometry is in meters.
One geoReference only; keep projection parameters canonical and use <offset> for recentering.
wrong: Writing raw UTM coordinates (~5e6 m) into geometry - CARLA/UE single-precision consumers lose cm accuracy.
Folding the offset into +x_0/+y_0 of the PROJ string.
Using lat/lon degrees as x/y.
Non-zero offset hdg (consumers disagree on order).
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 (8.5) adds the explicit world = R(hdg)*ODR + offset formulas and says to always apply the offset before converting with PROJ; recommends omitting heading. Example CRS given as EPSG:32632. Rule header.proj.max_one_proj carries a 1.9.0 id. <geoReference> and <offset> multiplicity 0..1 each.
figures: Figure 18: geoReference and offset - OpenDRIVE x/y near origin plus x/y offset equals georeferenced x/y (e.g. ~500000/40000 m); lesson: offset is ADDED to file coordinates to get projected coordinates.

sections.title: Geometry overview
sections.summary: The reference line is composed of planView geometry primitives: line, spiral (clothoid, linear curvature), arc (constant curvature), poly3 (cubic polynomial, deprecated) and paramPoly3 (parametric cubic).
figures: Figure 19: the five geometry element types.

sections.title: Road reference line
sections.summary: Every road has exactly one reference line (<planView> with 1..* <geometry>), along which lanes, signals and objects are defined. Each <geometry> gives start s, x, y, hdg and length plus exactly one shape child. Reference-line direction does not imply driving direction; it usually runs in the road center but may be offset.

attributes.name: length
attributes.meaning: Length of the element's reference line (>0)

formulas.name: local arc parameter
formulas.expr: ds = s - geometry.s,  0 <= ds <= length
formulas.notes: All primitives are evaluated in ds.

formulas.name: s continuity
formulas.expr: geometry[i].s = sum_{j<i} geometry[j].length ; road.length = sum of all geometry lengths
formulas.notes: 1.9 rules s-value_sum (shall) and road.length_sum_geometries (should).

formulas.name: position continuity (no gaps)
formulas.expr: |end(geometry[i]) - (geometry[i+1].x, geometry[i+1].y)| ~ 0
formulas.notes: Spec gives no tolerance; aim for < 1e-6..1e-3 m.

formulas.name: heading continuity (no kinks)
formulas.expr: hdg_end(geometry[i]) == geometry[i+1].hdg (mod 2*pi)
formulas.notes: Recommended (should).

rules.text: Each road has a reference line.
Only one reference line per road.
<geometry> elements are listed in ascending s order.
A <geometry> contains exactly one shape element (line/spiral/arc/poly3/paramPoly3).
For roads connected without a junction, the new road's reference line starts at the contactPoint of its predecessor/successor; directions may be opposite.
No leaps/gaps in the reference line.
No kinks (heading jumps) in the reference line.
Each geometry's s equals the sum of the lengths of all preceding geometries.
Road @length equals the sum of all geometry lengths.

use_cases.how: Fit a G1 (ideally G2) chain of line/arc/spiral or paramPoly3 segments; write s cumulatively from exact lengths; set road @length to the exact sum.
End point of road A (contactPoint end) must equal start/end point of road B with matching (or opposite, if directions reverse) heading.

right: Accumulate s from the same double lengths you write (no independent rounding).
Choose reference-line direction freely (e.g. OSM way direction); lane sides follow from it.
Recompute start x,y,hdg of each geometry from the end of the previous one to avoid drift.
wrong: Gaps between consecutive geometries or between connected roads.
Heading kinks at polyline vertices (raw polyline as chain of <line>s) - allowed only as 'should not'; causes lane-border spikes.
Two shape children in one <geometry>.
Zero/negative lengths.

sections.title: Straight line
sections.summary: <line> has no attributes; the reference line goes straight from (x,y) along hdg for length.

formulas.name: line evaluation
formulas.expr: x(ds) = x0 + ds*cos(hdg0) ; y(ds) = y0 + ds*sin(hdg0) ; hdg(ds) = hdg0 ; k = 0
formulas.notes: Exact.

sections.title: Spiral
sections.summary: <spiral> is a clothoid whose curvature changes linearly with arc length from curvStart to curvEnd over @length; used to transition between line and arc (or arcs of different curvature) without curvature jumps. Line/spiral/arc sequences can describe complex curvature profiles.

formulas.name: clothoid curvature
formulas.expr: k(ds) = curvStart + (curvEnd - curvStart) * ds / length
formulas.notes: Defining property in the spec.

formulas.name: curvature rate
formulas.expr: c' = (curvEnd - curvStart) / length
formulas.notes: Clothoid parameter A = 1/sqrt(|c'|).

formulas.name: spiral heading
formulas.expr: hdg(ds) = hdg0 + curvStart*ds + 0.5*c'*ds^2
formulas.notes: Integral of curvature.

formulas.name: spiral position
formulas.expr: x(ds) = x0 + integral_0^ds cos(hdg(tau)) dtau ; y(ds) = y0 + integral_0^ds sin(hdg(tau)) dtau
formulas.notes: Evaluate via Fresnel integrals or high-order numeric quadrature.

formulas.name: standard clothoid via Fresnel (odrSpiral)
formulas.expr: standard clothoid with zero curvature at l=0: X(l) = A*sqrt(pi)*C(l/(A*sqrt(pi))), Y(l) = sign(c')*A*sqrt(pi)*S(l/(A*sqrt(pi))), theta(l) = c'*l^2/2
formulas.vars: C,S Fresnel integrals C(z)=int_0^z cos(pi t^2/2)dt, S(z)=int_0^z sin(pi t^2/2)dt; A=1/sqrt(|c'|)
formulas.notes: For curvStart != 0: shift along the standard clothoid to l0 = curvStart/c', compute points at l0 and l0+ds, transform the difference by rotation R(hdg0 - theta(l0)) and add (x0,y0). If c'==0 fall back to arc/line.

rules.text: curvStart and curvEnd differ (otherwise use line or arc).

sections.title: Arc
sections.summary: <arc> has constant curvature over the element; positive curvature turns left.

formulas.name: arc heading
formulas.expr: hdg(ds) = hdg0 + k*ds

formulas.name: arc position
formulas.expr: x(ds) = x0 + (sin(hdg0 + k*ds) - sin(hdg0)) / k ; y(ds) = y0 - (cos(hdg0 + k*ds) - cos(hdg0)) / k
formulas.notes: For |k*ds| tiny use series / line to avoid cancellation.

formulas.name: arc center
formulas.expr: xc = x0 - sin(hdg0)/k ; yc = y0 + cos(hdg0)/k ; R = 1/|k|

sections.title: Cubic polynom (poly3, deprecated)
sections.summary: Deprecated since 1.6 (attributes deprecated 1.8). v(u) = a + b*u + c*u^2 + d*u^3 in a local u/v frame aligned with s/t at (x,y,hdg) when a=b=0; non-zero b rotates the start tangent by arctan(b), non-zero a shifts the frame origin along v so that (x,y) lies on the v axis. u runs from 0 to the projection of the end point onto the u axis (NOT arc length).

attributes.name: b
attributes.meaning: Polynom parameter b (start slope; arctan(b) = start angle in u/v)

formulas.name: global cubic (background)
formulas.expr: y(x) = a + b*x + c*x^2 + d*x^3
formulas.notes: Not usable for arbitrary orientations (Figure 27).

formulas.name: local cubic
formulas.expr: v(u) = a + b*u + c*u^2 + d*u^3
formulas.vars: u in [0, u_end]; u_end = projection of end point on u axis

formulas.name: u/v to x/y (a=b=0, Figure 28)
formulas.expr: beta = hdg + arctan(v(u)/u) ; x(u) = x0 + sqrt(u^2 + v(u)^2)*cos(beta) ; y(u) = y0 + sqrt(u^2 + v(u)^2)*sin(beta)
formulas.notes: Equivalent to x = x0 + u*cos(hdg) - v*sin(hdg), y = y0 + u*sin(hdg) + v*cos(hdg).

formulas.name: u/v to x/y (common implementation, any a,b)
formulas.expr: x = x0 + u*cos(hdg) - v(u)*sin(hdg) ; y = y0 + u*sin(hdg) + v(u)*cos(hdg)
formulas.notes: Used by most tools (esmini, libOpenDRIVE); with a!=0 the curve starts at (x0,y0)+a*N_left, i.e. NOT at (x,y) - conflicts with the spec rule that (x,y) lies on the v axis at u=0. Avoid by writing a=b=0.

formulas.name: poly3 heading / curvature
formulas.notes: Standard plane-curve results.

formulas.name: poly3 arc length
formulas.expr: length = integral_0^{u_end} sqrt(1 + v'(u)^2) du
formulas.notes: Must be solved numerically to map s->u.

sections.title: Parametric cubic curve (paramPoly3)
sections.summary: u(p) and v(p) are independent cubics in a common parameter p, expressed in a local u/v frame, then rotated by hdg and translated to (x,y). p runs over [0,1] (pRange='normalized') or [0,length] (pRange='arcLength'). p is generally not arc length, even with arcLength; only endpoints coincide. Writers should align u/v with s/t: aU=aV=bV=0, bU>0.

attributes.name: pRange
attributes.meaning: arcLength: p in [0,@length]; normalized: p in [0,1] (coefficients then unitless/in m). Required in 1.9 table; older readers commonly default to normalized

formulas.name: u polynomial
formulas.expr: u(p) = aU + bU*p + cU*p^2 + dU*p^3

formulas.name: v polynomial
formulas.expr: v(p) = aV + bV*p + cV*p^2 + dV*p^3

formulas.name: p from ds
formulas.expr: arcLength: p = ds (approximation; exact only at p=0 and p=length) ; normalized: p = ds/length (approximation)
formulas.notes: Exact mapping requires inverting the arc-length integral; most tools use the linear map. Writers should parametrize near-arc-length (|u'|^2+|v'|^2 ~ const) so the approximation is good.

formulas.name: u/v to x/y (aligned frame, standard implementation)
formulas.expr: x(p) = x0 + u(p)*cos(hdg) - v(p)*sin(hdg) ; y(p) = y0 + u(p)*sin(hdg) + v(p)*cos(hdg)
formulas.notes: With aU=aV=0 the curve starts at (x0,y0). Figure 29/32 show the u/v frame origin offset by (aU,aV) from the start point when they are non-zero; tools differ - avoid by writing aU=aV=0.

formulas.name: tangent heading
formulas.expr: hdg(p) = hdg0 + atan2(v'(p), u'(p))
formulas.vars: u' = bU + 2cU p + 3dU p^2 ; v' = bV + 2cV p + 3dV p^2
formulas.notes: At p=0: hdg0 + atan2(bV,bU) (Figure 29: arctan(bV/bU)); hence bV=0, bU>0 makes the start tangent equal hdg.

formulas.name: curvature
formulas.notes: Standard parametric curvature.

formulas.name: arc length / length_match
formulas.expr: L = integral_0^{p_end} sqrt(u'(p)^2 + v'(p)^2) dp  (should equal @length)
formulas.notes: Use Gauss-Legendre/adaptive Simpson; rule length_match.

formulas.name: Hermite fit (writer)
formulas.expr: given start (0,0) dir (1,0) and end (uE,vE) heading phiE in local frame, normalized: aU=aV=0, bU=L0, bV=0, cU=3uE-2bU-L1*cos(phiE), dU=bU+L1*cos(phiE)-2uE, cV=3vE-L1*sin(phiE), dV=L1*sin(phiE)-2vE
formulas.notes: Standard cubic Hermite; derived, not from spec. To convert to pRange=arcLength with p=ds: divide b by L, c by L^2, d by L^3 (L=@length); choose L0=L1~L so bU~1.

sections.summary: The road network is a set of <road> elements, each running along exactly one reference line (planView). formulas.name: road length
formulas.expr: road@length = sum(geometry@length) (xy-plane arc length of reference line)

sections.title: Road linkage
sections.summary: Roads are connected via <link><predecessor/><successor/></link>. The predecessor attaches at the start of this road's reference line (s=0) and the successor at its end (s=length). A link target is a road (elementType, elementId, contactPoint) or a junction (elementType+elementId; virtual junctions also elementS+elementDir). Reference lines of linked roads must actually touch; gaps/overlaps in the reference line are prohibited, while lane-boundary gaps/overlaps at a kink are tolerated but should be avoided.

attributes.name: elementId
attributes.meaning: ID of linked road or junction.

attributes.name: contactPoint
attributes.meaning: Which end of the LINKED road touches this road: start = linked road's s=0, end = linked road's s=length. Required when elementType=road; not used for junctions.

attributes.name: elementS
attributes.meaning: Virtual junctions only: s on the linked road (not at its ends) where the connection is; only with elementType=road.

attributes.name: elementDir
attributes.meaning: Given with elementS: direction on the linked road (relative to its s) from which this road is entered.

formulas.name: connection points
formulas.expr: P_this = refline(this, 0) for predecessor, refline(this, this.length) for successor; P_other = refline(other, 0) if contactPoint=start else refline(other, other.length); require |P_this - P_other| ~ 0
formulas.notes: Recommended G1: same contactPoint pairing (start-start or end-end) implies headings differ by pi; end->start pairing implies equal headings. Elevation should match too.

formulas.name: reciprocal contactPoint
formulas.expr: A.successor=(road B, start) <=> B.predecessor=(road A, end); A.successor=(B, end) <=> B.successor=(A, end); A.predecessor=(B, start) <=> B.predecessor=(A, start); A.predecessor=(B, end) <=> B.successor=(A, start)
formulas.notes: Rule: which element (pred/succ) you write on A is set by A's end; the contactPoint is set by B's end. Matches Figure 36 tables.

sections.title: Methods of elevation (overview)
sections.summary: Road surface height is built from elevation along s (elevationProfile), the lateral profile in t (superelevation roll and/or shape), and objects that can raise road height. The s coordinate and road length never change because of elevation.

formulas.name: surface point (combined, derived)
formulas.expr: phi = sElev(s); z_ref = elev(s); h = hShape(s,t) (+ lane height); XY = refXY(s) + n(s)*(t*cos(phi) - h*sin(phi)); Z = z_ref + t*sin(phi) + h*cos(phi)
formulas.vars: n(s): unit left normal of reference line in xy; t measured in the rotated (superelevated) cross-section plane; h along the rotated up axis
formulas.notes: Derived from Figures 40/42: superelevation rolls the whole t-h frame about the reference line; positive phi lowers the right side (t<0). Plan-view offset is t*cos(phi): projected width shrinks, actual width kept. Many tools approximate with lateral=t.

rules.text: Elevation does not alter s length.

sections.title: Road elevation
sections.summary: <elevation> elements inside <elevationProfile> give the reference-line height (inertial z) as cubic polynomials in ds, valid from @s until the next element. Default elevation is 0 (what zero means depends on georeferencing).

formulas.name: elevation
formulas.expr: elev(ds) = a + b*ds + c*ds^2 + d*ds^3, ds = s - sStart
formulas.vars: elev: z of reference line; sStart: element @s

sections.summary: Superelevation is the roll angle (rad) of the whole cross section around the reference line, as a cubic in ds. Positive values make the road fall to the right (t<0 lower). It keeps actual lane width but reduces projected (plan-view) width; lanes can opt out via lane @level=true.

sections.summary: <shape> elements give detailed cross-section height as cubic polynomials in dt, starting at @t, grouped into profiles at given @s; several shapes per s cover different t ranges. sections.title: Road surface (OpenCRG)
sections.summary: <surface><CRG> references an OpenCRG curved-regular-grid file adding detailed elevation (or friction) to a road between sStart and sEnd. sections.title: Lanes (introduction, ids, center lane)
sections.summary: Every road carries lanes inside <lanes>. A zero-width center lane with id 0 is the numbering reference: ids ascend to the left (+t) and descend to the right (-t). Without a laneOffset the center lane coincides with the road reference line; on two-way roads it usually separates the driving directions, on one-way roads all lanes may sit on one side.

driving direction is derived from id sign and road rule (RHT: right lanes drive with s, left lanes against s; LHT reversed)
minimum road (1.7): center lane plus one lane with width > 0; 1.9 relaxes this (roads used as junction boundaries may have no width>0 lane)
<lanes> contains: laneOffset*, laneSection+ (1.9: <lanes> may be repeated with @layer permanent|temporary)

sections.title: Introduction: junction types and when to use each
sections.summary: A junction is the device for linking more than two road ends. 1.7 knows three types (common/default, direct, virtual); 1.8 adds crossing. The chapter gives a decision table mapping real-world situations to types, plus three global rules: junctions never overlap, direct junctions never carry @connectingRoad, default/virtual junctions never carry @linkedRoad.
concepts: Common junction (type='default'): drivable lanes of different paths may overlap; traffic can cross; paths are explicit connecting roads.
Direct junction (type='direct', 1.7+): traffic can change road (split/merge) but never crosses; roads are linked directly via @linkedRoad, no connecting roads.
Virtual junction (type='virtual'): the main road is not cut; side branches attach at an s-range of the main road.
Crossing (type='crossing', 1.8+): two or more roads cross on the same level but traffic cannot change between them (rail level crossing, ped/bike crossing).

sections.title: Junction elevation grid (1.8+)
sections.summary: <elevationGrid> gives a coarse square grid of z values laid out along the junction reference line (rows perpendicular to it, spaced gridSpacing, starting at sStart). Inside the boundary it overrides all road-derived elevation; lane heights are added on top; heights are bicubically interpolated, and a cubic blend over transitionLength joins incoming roads smoothly. Common junctions only; not a replacement for OpenCRG.
concepts: Row k is at s = sStart + k*gridSpacing on the junction reference line; centre value at t=0, left values at t = +gridSpacing, +2*gridSpacing ... (inside->outside), right values at t = -gridSpacing ...
Grid must extend by complete squares beyond the boundary in all directions; minimum is 4 points forming a bounding square (constant z = flat plane).
Roads crossing the grid outside the boundary keep their own elevation; inside, grid wins (connecting roads are inside so grid always applies to them).
Lane height (sidewalk kerb) is superimposed on grid z.

attributes.name: sStart
attributes.meaning: s of first row on the junction reference line.

attributes.name: center
attributes.meaning: z on the reference line for this row.

attributes.name: left
attributes.meaning: z values to the left, inside to outside.

attributes.name: right
attributes.meaning: z values to the right, inside to outside.

formulas.name: grid point position
formulas.expr: P(k,j) = refline(s = sStart + k*g) + t*n, t = j*g (j>0 left, j<0 right)
formulas.vars: g = gridSpacing; n = left normal of reference line; k = row index (<elevation> order)
formulas.notes: Inferred from rules (rows perpendicular to the reference line, spacing g); the spec does not print this formula.

formulas.name: edge cubic
formulas.expr: f(x) = d x^3 + c x^2 + b x + a
formulas.vars: fitted along grid lines through neighbouring points
formulas.notes: Used to obtain tangents; c=d=0 if not enough support points (rule polynome_coefficient_values).

formulas.name: bicubic patch
formulas.expr: alpha = A * [[Z, Tt],[Ts, Tst]] * A^T ; z(s,t) = [1 s s^2 s^3] * alpha * [1 t t^2 t^3]^T
formulas.vars: Z = 2x2 corner z values; Ts, Tt, Tst = 2x2 partial derivatives in s, t, st at corners; A = constant 4x4 bicubic Hermite matrix; s,t normalised to [0,1] within the square
formulas.notes: Standard bicubic interpolation (12.11.1). A = [[1,0,0,0],[0,0,1,0],[-3,3,-2,-1],[2,-2,1,1]] in standard form.

formulas.name: transition polygon parameterisation
formulas.expr: A = P0 + k (P1 - P0); B = P3 + k (P2 - P3); P = A + l (B - A); solve fx(k,l)=0, fy(k,l)=0
formulas.vars: P0..P3 corners of the transition quad from the joint segment and adjacent lane segments (transitionLength)

formulas.name: road-to-grid blend
formulas.expr: z_P(l) = a + b l + c l^2 + d l^3; a = zA; b = mA; c = -3 zA + 3 zB - 2 mA - mB; d = 2 zA - 2 zB + mA + mB
formulas.vars: zA, mA: road elevation and slope at the road end (A side); zB, mB: grid z and slope along AB at B; slopes scaled by |AB|; l in [0,1]
formulas.notes: Cubic Hermite. Spec text labels the grid slope mA in one place - typo for mB.

sections.title: Objects - introduction and <object>
sections.summary: Objects are items that expand, delimit or supplement a road (parking spaces, crosswalks, barriers, buildings, trees, poles). Each object belongs to exactly one <road> (inside <road>/<objects>), is placed at an origin (s,t,zOffset) in that road's reference-line frame, and is rotated by hdg/pitch/roll into a local u/v/z frame. Its extent is an angular box (length,width,height) or a cylinder (radius,height). An <outline> (or 1.8+ <skeleton>) refines and supersedes the box but must stay inside it. Objects never move: 'dynamic' only means they have moving parts, such as tunnel fans or wind turbines.
concepts: object = static road furniture tied to one road (road-relative, not inertial)
angular bounding box (length/width/height) vs circular (radius/height) - mutually exclusive, chosen by which attributes are present
local u/v/z frame (spec 6.4): u forward (= s at hdg 0), v left (= t), z up; rotations applied heading -> pitch (about v') -> roll (about u'')
orientation (+/-/none) is traffic-direction validity only; it does NOT rotate the object (hdg does)
validLength: extent of validity along s (0 = point object)
perpToRoad=true makes the object follow the road surface normal and ignores pitch/roll (new in 1.7)
dynamic=yes: object has movable parts but fixed position
only small objects may rely on a single insertion point on a curved elevation (Figure 90)
1.7 axis caveat: 1.7 table text says length along v and width along u; 1.9 corrects this to length along u (forward) and width along v (lateral). Use the 1.9 meaning.

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: unique id within the whole file

attributes.name: s
attributes.meaning: s of object origin on the parent road

attributes.name: t
attributes.meaning: t of object origin (lateral from reference line, not from laneOffset)

attributes.name: zOffset
attributes.meaning: origin height relative to reference-line elevation at s

attributes.name: type
attributes.meaning: category. 1.7/1.8 XSD values: none, obstacle, pole, tree, vegetation, barrier, building, parkingSpace, patch, railing, trafficIsland, crosswalk, streetLamp, gantry, soundBarrier, roadMark, roadSurface(1.8), plus deprecated car, van, bus, trailer, bike, motorbike, tram, train, pedestrian, wind. 1.8 deprecates patch->roadSurface, railing/soundBarrier->barrier, streetLamp/wind->pole

attributes.meaning: variant of type (1.8+ defines subtype tables, e.g. barrier/guardRail, pole/trafficLight, crosswalk/zebra, roadMark/arrowLeft)

attributes.name: dynamic
attributes.meaning: yes = has movable parts; default no

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.meaning: + valid for travel in +s, - for -s, none for both; does not affect heading. Use +/- only if the object affects traffic rules

attributes.name: hdg
attributes.meaning: heading relative to road direction at s (0 = along +s)

attributes.name: pitch
attributes.meaning: pitch relative to x/y plane, applied after hdg

attributes.name: roll
attributes.meaning: roll relative to x/y plane, applied after pitch

attributes.name: perpToRoad
attributes.meaning: true: object perpendicular to road surface everywhere, pitch/roll ignored; default false

attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local u (1.9 wording; 1.7 text says v)

attributes.name: width
attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local v (1.9 wording; 1.7 text says u)

attributes.name: height
attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local z, upward from origin

attributes.name: radius
attributes.meaning: cylinder radius in u/v; alternative to length+width

attributes.name: validLength
attributes.meaning: validity along s; 0 for point object

attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: physically invalidated (e.g. crossed out); traffic should ignore; default false

attributes.name: temporary
attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: temporary placement (road works); default false

formulas.name: object origin (inertial)
formulas.expr: x0 = xr(s) - t*sin(th(s)); y0 = yr(s) + t*cos(th(s)); z0 = zr(s) + zOffset
formulas.vars: xr,yr,th = reference-line point and heading at s (planView); zr = elevation profile at s; t = lateral offset from the reference line
formulas.notes: t is NOT shifted by laneOffset. In 1.7 zOffset is relative to reference-line elevation; superelevation/shape are not included. On a superelevated road, the surface height at t differs from zr(s), so a writer that wants objects on the surface must add that difference to zOffset itself.

formulas.name: object world heading
formulas.expr: H = th(s) + hdg; then pitch about v', then roll about u''
formulas.vars: th(s) road heading at s, hdg object attribute
formulas.notes: heading 0 = object u-axis along +s. Rotation R = Rz(H)*Ry(pitch)*Rx(roll), ISO 8855 right-handed (u fwd, v left, z up)

formulas.name: local -> inertial
formulas.expr: [x,y,z] = [x0,y0,z0] + Rz(H)*Ry(pitch)*Rx(roll)*[u,v,z]
formulas.vars: u,v,z local coords of a box corner, cornerLocal or vertexLocal
formulas.notes: with perpToRoad=true, replace pitch/roll by the road-surface orientation (slope + superelevation) at (s,t)

formulas.name: angular bounding box
formulas.expr: u in [-length/2,+length/2], v in [-width/2,+width/2], z in [0,height]
formulas.notes: 1.7 has no explicit formula. Centring the box on the origin in u/v, with z from 0 to height, is a common tool convention, not normative; document the choice.

formulas.name: cylinder
formulas.expr: u^2+v^2 <= radius^2, z in [0,height]
formulas.notes: circular object

The object origin is given in s/t coordinates of its road.
Circular (radius) and angular (length/width) shapes are mutually exclusive; the attributes used define the shape.
Objects placed via elevation/lateral profiles should be small enough not to cut into or float above the road surface, and not to skew OpenCRG surfaces.
If an outline exists, it supersedes the bounding box, but all its points must lie inside the box.

sections.summary: <repeat> clones an object along the road: discrete instances every 'distance' metres, or, with distance=0, one continuous extruded feature (guard rail, wall). sections.title: Object outline (outlines, cornerRoad, cornerLocal)
sections.summary: An <outline> is a polygon or polyline of corner points with per-corner heights. It is used for traffic islands, irregular parking spaces, special markings and buildings. Corners are either all <cornerRoad> (s,t,dz in road coordinates) or all <cornerLocal> (u,v,z in the object's local frame), with at least two per outline. Several outlines per object are allowed via <outlines> (tree trunk + crown, pole + lamp head, logical sub-areas of an island). Readers must still accept a 1.4-style <outline> placed directly under <object>.

laneType: how the application treats the area (e.g. sidewalk, border)
the outline supersedes the bounding box but must fit inside it
cornerRoad: road-relative points that follow curvature; good for shapes along the road
cornerLocal: rigid shape relative to object origin + hdg; good for buildings and islands
outline/corner ids are needed for markings and borders (cornerReference, outlineId)

elements.notes: wrapper; 1.4 files may have <outline> directly under <object>

attributes.name: dz

formulas.name: cornerRoad to inertial
formulas.expr: x = xr(s_i) - t_i*sin(th(s_i)); y = yr(s_i) + t_i*cos(th(s_i)); zBase = zr(s_i) + dz_i; zTop = zBase + height_i
formulas.notes: object hdg/pitch/roll do NOT apply to cornerRoad points

formulas.name: cornerLocal to inertial
formulas.expr: [x,y,zBase] = O + Rz(th(s)+hdg) * [u_i, v_i, z_i] (pitch/roll also applied if non-zero); zTop = zBase + height_i
formulas.notes: Figure 96 example: P(s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0), hdg=7pi/4

formulas.expr: q(p) = q_i + (q_{i+1}-q_i)*p, p in [0,1], computed in inertial coordinates (cornerRoad) or local coordinates (cornerLocal)
formulas.notes: cornerRoad edges are straight in x/y, NOT curved along the road, so add corners on curves

sections.title: Signal positioning (logical vs physical)
sections.summary: In 1.7 a signal's s/t is its logical position, i.e. where it takes effect on the road it governs. If the physical mast stands elsewhere (across the junction, hanging over it, or on another road), it can be described by exactly one of <positionRoad> (roadId,s,t,zOffset,hOffset) or <positionInertial> (x,y,z,hdg). Positioning never changes the signal's content. 1.8 deprecates this: signals sit at their physical location, and relations are expressed with <reference>/<dependency>.

sections.title: Controllers (and junction controllers)
sections.summary: A top-level <controller> groups dynamic signals that always share the same state (for example all lights of one phase) through <control signalId>. A <junction> lists its controllers with <controller id sequence> to order them. Phase timings are not in OpenDRIVE (OpenSCENARIO or the application provides them). Unlike dependencies, controllers are high-level and independent of other signals.

sections.title: Country codes, types, dynamic signals (cross-cutting notes)

sections.title: Signal boards (1.8+, not in 1.7)
sections.summary: 1.8 adds boards so that one <signal> can carry several signs. A <staticBoard> contains <sign> children positioned by local v/z on the board (type='staticBoard', dynamic=false). A <vmsBoard> is a variable message board with <displayArea>s (type='vmsBoard', dynamic=true). A multiBoard mixes both. <vmsGroup>/<vmsBoardReference> group VMS boards on one gantry.

sections.title: Signal semantics (1.8+, not in 1.7)
sections.summary: <semantics> gives a country-independent meaning to a signal, so simulators need not decode national catalogues. Children include <speed type value unit> (maximum, minimum, recommended, zone, plus End variants), <priority type> (stop, yield, trafficLight, stopLine, priorityRoad, 4way...), <lane type>, <prohibited>, <warning>, <parking>, <routing>, <streetname>, <tourist> and supplementary qualifiers (allows, prohibits, distance, time, environment, explanatory). 1.9 adds traffic participants <vehicle>, <person> and <animal>.

sections.title: Railroads - introduction
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE models trams and streetcars only where rails meet roads; it does not cover complex rail networks or rail signalling. Rails live on roads: each track is its own <road>, and <road>/<railroad> holds switches. In 1.9, switches are the only rail-specific element; tracks use <road> and signals use <signal>.

rules.text: Each railway track requires its own road (one tram/rail lane per road).

sections.title: Switches (mainTrack, sideTrack, partner)
sections.summary: <switch> on a track's <railroad> splits it into two directions. It is dynamic (operable during simulation) or static (fixed 'straight' or 'turn'). <mainTrack id s dir> gives the switch point on the main track; <sideTrack id s dir> gives the branch road. Two switches joined by a side track are partners and must be set consistently.
